sessions.title: Dataverse Hidden Gems with Model-Driven Apps
sessions.abstract:
1. Power of Currency
Multi-currency awareness is one of Dataverse’s most under-used strengths.
Each record stores both transaction currency and base currency values—auto-converted using the organization’s exchange rates.
Hidden gem: even roll-up and calculated fields respect the base-currency context.
Demo idea → show how a USD-based record dynamically recalculates when the system currency rate changes.
2. Relationship Behavior
Relationships aren’t just for lookups—they define cascade behavior.
Hidden gem: fine-tune how Assign, Share, Delete, Merge cascade between parent–child records.
Example: Prevent automatic cascade delete from Account → Invoice, but still allow cascade assign.
Pro tip → switch to “Configurable cascading” instead of the legacy all-or-nothing rules to avoid unwanted data loss.
3. Activity Table Magic
All emails, phone calls, tasks, appointments, notes, and custom activities share a single base Activity table.
Hidden gem: unified timeline + filters = 360° communication view across related entities.
Power users can create custom activity types (e.g., “Onsite Visit”) that automatically appear in the timeline.
Combine with activity party table to track multiple participants.
4. Vibe Coding
A modern approach to designing model-driven apps that “feel alive.”
Hidden gem: leverage business rules + Power Fx + Command Designer to add logic without plugins.
Use JavaScript events and custom command bar buttons for richer UX—keep business logic in the Dataverse layer…

sessions.abstract:

Then Microsoft made up new words and released Translytical Flows that use Microsoft Fabric's User Defined Functions to open up the possibilities. The possibilities are endless!
In this session we will demo building this new feature from scratch along side a demo of a simple Power App doing the same write back. Then we will have the fun of comparing the functionality, useability and maybe even the licencing. Who will win?
Plenty of demos, audience participation and time for questions.

sessions.title: The Magic of Merging: Getting Friendly with Power Query Joins in Power BI
sessions.abstract:
Ever hit a roadblock when trying to shape or enrich your data in Power BI? Let's shine the spotlight on Power Query Joins. These aren’t just the VLOOKUPs and XLOOKUPs from our Excel days in a fancy new suit. They're the powerhouse tools that help you mold and enhance your data, setting the stage for some killer analyses later on.
In our upcoming session, we're going hands-on with these joining wonders. We'll break down the usual join suspects and then venture into the shadows where the mysterious seventh type lurks. From fuzzy-matching fun to multi-column join shenanigans, we're covering it all. But here's the thing: it's not just about making datasets play nice together. It's about pulling in rich details, filling in gaps, and creating that perfect dataset that makes your analyses pop.
By the time we call it a wrap, you'll be all set to use Power Query Joins like a pro. They'll be your secret weapon in crafting and refining data in Power BI, setting you up for smoother, more insightful analyses. Ready to master the merging magic? Let’s dive in and shape some data!

sessions.title: DAX Demystified: 5 Key Lessons Every Beginner Needs to Learn Early
sessions.abstract:

In this session, Markus Ehrenmueller-Jensen shares five essential lessons he wishes he’d known when he first started with DAX. You’ll gain clarity on the fundamental concepts that often trip up beginners, like the critical difference between calculated columns and measures, and the game-changing role of row context vs. filter context. Markus will guide you through real examples and practical tips to help you understand and manipulate context—the heart of DAX—to create powerful, dynamic calculations.
Whether you're just getting started or already building models, this session will give you a solid foundation and a few "aha!" moments that make DAX finally click.
Who Should Attend:
Power BI users, data analysts, and Excel pros beginning their DAX journey—or anyone who's written a measure that didn’t quite work and wondered why.

sessions.title: How Data Agents in Fabric can answer questions not available in existing reports
sessions.abstract:
Data Agents in Microsoft Fabric allow for end users to ask any question against your data sitting inside Microsoft Fabric. Very often a report cannot cater for all reporting requirements. This is where Data Agents excel because they can answer interesting questions, allow the author to customize the experience.
○ In this session I will show you how to set up and configure the Data Agent which will include the following:
§ What is a data agent and why you should look to use it in your organization.
§ Required tenant settings
§ Selecting the data sources which will be a Lakehouse and Semantic Model
§ Ask some basic questions
§ Data Agent Configuration
§ Sharing the Data Agent
§ Consuming the Data Agent in other applications.
Questions

sessions.title: Building a True Single Source of Truth In Microsoft Fabric with OneLake
sessions.abstract: In this session, we explore how Microsoft Fabric and OneLake enable organizations to create a unified, secure, and scalable single source of truth for all their data needs. We’ll demystify how OneLake centralizes data across analytics workloads, data engineering, data warehousing, real-time analytics, and BI, while eliminating silos, reducing duplication, and simplifying governance. Through practical concepts and real-world scenarios, attendees will learn how to design a cohesive data foundation that powers reliable insights, consistent metrics, and smarter decision-making across the business. Perfect for data engineers, analysts, and decision-makers looking to modernize their analytics ecosystem.

sessions.title: Keynote: Become a Frontier Firm: Why AI Transformation Is a Training Program, Not a Tool implementation
sessions.abstract:
Buying a gym membership does not make you fit. It only gives you access.
The same is true for AI.
Many organizations adopt Copilot and expect transformation to happen automatically. Frontier firms think differently. They understand that AI transformation is not about deploying tools, but about training new ways of working.
In this keynote, you will explore how Copilot and Copilot Agents change work only when they are treated like a structured training program: building the right foundation, improving technique, increasing autonomy, and integrating AI into daily routines. Using a clear fitness analogy, this talk reframes AI adoption from a technology initiative into a performance discipline.
This keynote is about mindset, habits, and leadership decisions that separate experimentation from real transformation.

sessions.title: Keynote: The Agentic Decade. How we redefine work, skills & leadership
sessions.abstract:
The Agentic Decade is here and it’s transforming everything we know about work. We are moving from task-based productivity to a world where AI agents run processes, make decisions, and reshape how organisations operate.
In this 30-minute session, Femke shares where the Agentic Workplace is heading, which skills will define the next generation of professionals, and why community and continuous learning matter more than ever. You’ll discover how roles evolve when AI becomes a teammate, how to design agent-ready workflows, and what leaders must do to stay ahead.
A fast, practical and inspiring session for anyone who wants to stay relevant in a world where agents don’t just support your work.. they run it.

sessions.title: Anatomy of an agent
sessions.abstract: What actually is an agent? While the term has been increasingly used across the industry, the reality of what it means can be very different, depending on who and when you speak to someone (especially Microsoft). The excitement of what can happen is often swiftly followed by a confusion of what will actually happen. This session will break apart the anatomy of what an agent is and talk through the different components of the modern, AI powered capabilities and show you what you need to consider. It will explain the building blocks needed and lead you towards how the decisions on those blocks can help you understand which technologies to use when. With each of these, you will see what different technologies are available and how you can choose what to use when. You will learn: - What are the building blocks of an agent - How do you design your agent to provide the right value - What technology is available to build agents for end users, power users and specialists - When you don’t need an agent - How to be a responsible agent builder I will talk focus on Copilot Studio agents, Copilot Studio Lite/Declarative Agents and Microsoft Foundry with a little of the SharePoint agents and may even sprinkle in a little Salesforce Agentforce. Remember, if your agent is not from the region of generative AI, it is just sparkling automation

sessions.title: Copilot Agents with MCP Servers: The Good, The Bad and the Ugly
sessions.abstract: This session dives into the evolving landscape of Copilot Studio agents integrated with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. It highlights the advantages of connecting agents to external systems for richer, more contextual outputs that transform enterprise workflows. Participants will uncover common pitfalls in security, scalability, and governance when deploying these advanced agents in production. Real-life implementation stories will reveal both the brilliance and the breaking points of this new architecture. Attendees will leave with practical frameworks for balancing innovation, compliance, and control in MCP-powered Copilot ecosystems.

sessions.title: Building a Robust Copilot Studio Strategy
sessions.abstract:
As Copilot Studio adoption accelerates, organizations must move beyond ad-hoc agent creation and establish a well-architected, enterprise-grade strategy. This session dives deep into the technical foundations required to design, deploy, and operate Copilot Studio at scale.
We will examine core architectural decisions, including environment and tenant strategy, Dataverse and data source design, authentication and authorization models, connector usage and isolation, and secure integration patterns with Power Platform, Microsoft 365, and external APIs. The session also covers agent lifecycle management, versioning, ALM pipelines, monitoring, telemetry, and compliance considerations in regulated environments.
Using concrete architecture patterns and real-world scenarios, this talk provides hands-on guidance for building Copilot Studio agents that are secure by default, observable, governable, and resilient. Attendees will gain a practical reference architecture and decision framework to support production-grade AI agents aligned with enterprise security, governance, and platform best practices.

sessions.title: Navigating the Era of M365 AI Agents: From Copilot to Enterprise‑Scale Agent Ecosystems
sessions.abstract: We are entering a new phase of Microsoft 365 transformation: the shift from AI assistants to full‑fledged AI agents. With innovations like Work IQ, Agent 365, Copilot Studio multi‑agent orchestration, and dozens of purpose‑built agents across Microsoft 365, organizations now face both massive opportunity and new governance challenges. This session equips business leaders, architects, and IT professionals with a practical roadmap to adopt, scale, and govern AI agents in Microsoft 365.

sessions.title: Bohemian Card-sody in Copilot Studio: Level up your agents’ UI/ UX game with Adaptive Cards
sessions.abstract:
Agent building without considering end-users’ experience is like trying to play Bohemian Rhapsody on a broken guitar—chaotic, messy, and frustrating for everyone involved. Developers often jump in full of enthusiasm, only to face messy outputs, poorly summarized data, and automation flows that leave users scratching their heads. Without a solid design, human-in-the-loop strategies, and testing, your outputs can miss all the right notes.
The key to success? Leveraging Adaptive Cards with clarity, formatting outputs effectively, and keeping humans in the loop for critical interactions. Testing your cards in advance and embedding them seamlessly in Power Apps, Power Automate, or Power Pages ensures your automation flows feel smooth, intuitive, and ready for prime time. With the right approach, your Copilot Studio cards can hit the perfect UX chord every time.
In this session, I’ll guide you through the key elements of Adaptive Card mastery in Copilot Studio. You’ll see live demos, learn best practices for card design and output summarization, explore human-in-the-loop automation patterns, test like a pro, and embed your cards into real applications. Walk away ready to turn your Adaptive Cards into a rock solid, crowd-pleasing experience.

sessions.title: Scaling AI Agents Securely: Next-Level Governance for Power Platform Admins
sessions.abstract:
Power Platform admins have mastered the essentials: environment strategy, DLP, Purview, and Copilot Studio governance. But Microsoft is now introducing a new layer of controls that will reshape how AI agents are identified, secured, and managed across the tenant—Agent 365, Entra Agent ID, and the Azure Foundry Control Plane.
This session looks at what these changes actually mean in practice. We’ll explore the new risks and opportunities they introduce, how agent identities and cross-platform registries shift the governance model, and what needs to change in your existing processes.
You’ll learn how to adapt your governance approach in areas such as:
- Using Agent 365 as a central registry for AI agent inventory and risk classification
- Integrating Entra Agent ID into identity and access governance
- Understanding what Power Platform admins need to know about the Foundry Control Plane and how it supports hybrid and advanced AI agents
- Updating onboarding, approval, monitoring, incident response, and decommissioning workflows for AI agents at scale
Whether you oversee Copilot Studio agents or broader Microsoft 365 AI capabilities, you’ll leave with a clear view of how these new services fit together and how to evolve your governance model as your AI footprint grows.

sessions.title: Extremely Accurate AI: Leveraging Azure AI Search, MCP & Foundry with Copilot Studio
sessions.abstract:
AI doesn't have to be a “Black Box”. With just a few Azure tools you can take complete control over what AI is doing and get the exact results you expect....EVERY TIME.
This all-demo session will showcase how the right combination of Azure AI Search, MCP, Azure Functions and Azure AI Foundry, can consistently give exact results in Copilot Studio and Power Automate.
These techniques aren’t theoretical! They’re what took our AI practice from distrusting, to being essential for how our business runs today.
Part 1: Azure AI Search
After configuring AI Search live, we’ll show example after example of how AI search outperforms OOTB Copilot Studio connectors both in speed and accuracy
Part 2: Complex Queries WITH Complex Transparency
When you need to ask Dataverse complicated questions, you need to get creative. We’ll build an Azure function that leverages the TDS endpoint in Dataverse, and can answer complex questions about your data, even ones that fetchXML can’t handle!
Part 3: AI Foundry
Having a Copilot is nice but what if you had a Clone-pilot? i.e. an agent that sounded exactly like you who could respond to questions, so you don’t have to. We’ll explore fine-tuning in Azure AI Foundry that literally uses your data (not prompts), to sound like you, and not a robot.
Part 4: MCP
Model-context protocol seems to replace much of what the Copilot Studio connectors used to offer, especially around Dataverse, but we'll separate fact from fiction.

sessions.title: How Copilot Studio Turned Me Into an AI Agent Believer
sessions.abstract:
Building AI agents wasn’t always easy—early chatbot development felt convoluted, rigid, and at times, discouraging. I questioned whether AI-powered assistants would ever truly deliver on their promise.
But with Copilot Studio, everything changed. The latest advancements—adaptive conversations, seamless data integration, and a more intuitive design—have made agent building smarter and more powerful than ever.
In this session, I’ll share my journey from skepticism to excitement, highlighting how Copilot Studio reignited my belief in AI agents. If you’ve ever felt frustrated by bot development, this session will show you why now is the time to believe again.
Key items covered in this session are:
1) Different agent building options in Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365.
2) Use generative AI to determine how best to respond to users and events.
3) When to use off-the-shelf versus tailored agents.
Navigate through licenses by understanding the requirements first.

sessions.title: A Deep Dive into Copilot Studio Agents
sessions.abstract:
A Deeper dive into Creating Copilot Studio Agents by leveraging system topics, creating fallbacks, tools, MCP servers, open api integrations and more.
Learn how to dynamically scope retrieval of knowledge and accessing grounded data using Copilot API.

sessions.title: Staying on Topic (Literally) in Copilot Studio
sessions.abstract: This session is focused on the Topics functionality in Copilot Studio. In his session will discuss everything around topics, like questions, messages, adaptive cards, calling tools, etc. I will show how to build topics, restrict them and how to use them when building an agent live.

sessions.title: When AI Starts Acting: Securing and Governing Agent Fleets in Microsoft 365
sessions.abstract:
Abstract (WHAT, WHY, HOW, WHO)
WHAT: AI is moving from copilots that draft to agents that execute. This session shows how to design, secure, and govern an enterprise “agent fleet” across Microsoft 365, Security, and AI, using a practical blueprint and a real-world scenario.
WHY: The biggest enterprise risk is not model capability, it’s what happens when an agent’s output turns into action under pressure. Without explicit decision rights, auditability, and a control plane, governance becomes visible only after something goes wrong.
HOW: We will walk through a concrete end-to-end example: an AI agent resolves an IT ServiceNow ticket (VPN breaks after an update). You’ll see how agent identity and least privilege are enforced, how sensitive data access is governed, how tool calls are controlled, and how monitoring and incident response work for agent actions.
WHO: Built for M365 admins, security professionals, architects, and developers who want actionable patterns to move from pilots to production (level 200–300).

sessions.title: Keynote: Navigating the Azure AI seas
sessions.abstract:
Let's check out the expansive world of Azure AI services! This session is designed to showcase the breadth of Azure’s AI capabilities and how they can be applied to various real-world scenarios. With mostly demos I'll get you situated in what's available and how to get started and how to continue with your AI use cases. This session will provide valuable insights into choosing the right Azure AI services for your needs.
We’ll explore the ocean of services, including the Cognitive services for vision, speech, and language understanding, as well as Azure OpenAI to utilize Generative AI and Azure Machine Learning for managing your Machine Learning project lifecycle. Through demos in Microsoft Foundry, you’ll see these services in action, solving common business challenges.
I'll let you sneak peek at some use cases where Azure AI has been used, providing you with real examples as inspiration. After this session, you'll have a better understanding of how Azure AI can enhance your applications and the confidence to start testing and implementing these services in your own projects.

sessions.title: From Models to Agents: Engineering Custom Engine Agents in Microsoft Foundry
sessions.abstract:
Microsoft Foundry introduces a powerful platform for building Custom Engine Agents that can reason, take actions, use tools, and work with enterprise data.
In this session, you’ll learn the architecture behind Engine Agents and how to design, build, test, and deploy them using Foundry’s modern agent development environment.
We’ll walk through real examples showing tool integration, grounding with enterprise data, and best practices for production-ready agents that accelerate business workflows.

sessions.title: PIMp your administration
sessions.abstract:
Zero Trust in relation to identity and administration is a critical topic that leaves no room for error.
Privileged Identity Management (PIM) is a modern and essential technology that provides significant security benefits in this space.
In this session, I’ll explore strategies for implementing and using PIM effectively, and how it integrates with other Entra technologies such as Conditional Access Policies and Protected Actions.
While PIM is a key focus of the talk, there’s more to strengthening your administrative posture. In the second part, I’ll highlight recent developments and share field-tested recommendations, including updates to Administrative Units and the integration of Security Copilot into Entra, along with the practical value it brings.
All topics will be illustrated with hands-on demos to ensure real-world relevance and applicability.

sessions.title: Azure Verified Modules and private modules: a powerful combo
sessions.abstract:
In the rapidly evolving landscape of cloud infrastructure, the Azure Bicep stands out as a declarative language and a tool designed to simplify the deployment of Azure resources.
In this session, we will explore the world of Bicep modules that are published to Microsoft’s Public Registry through the Azure Verified Modules (AVM) initiative and how they can be combined with private modules that organizations can develop to fit their specific needs.
We will focus on a practical example on how to build a ‘Private Modules Registry’, a publishing engine on GitHub that can follow recommended practice for testing and validating your modules before they are published to your private registry.
The goal is to demonstrate how you can combine the use of public modules, curated by Microsoft, with your own code in a consistent way and how to empower your cloud engineers to use this Library.
The demo environment (and repository) will contain all code artifacts for building the Private Modules Library, provisioning all necessary prerequisites, and deploying a ‘solution’ using a private pattern module.

sessions.title: Secure Your Copilot Studio Deployments
sessions.abstract: Learn how to secure and govern Copilot Studio agents at enterprise scale. See how Microsoft IT does it, explore key governance pillars, and watch live demos on auditing, maker protection, and Power Platform controls—all designed to keep your AI safe, compliant, and enterprise-ready.

sessions.title: Manual Power Shell vs. Scriptrunner
sessions.abstract: In this session, we explored the practical differences between running PowerShell manually and using ScriptRunner as an enterprise automation platform. We discussed how manual PowerShell execution offers full flexibility and direct control for administrators, but often results in fragmented script management, inconsistent execution standards, and limited governance. ScriptRunner, on the other hand, centralizes all scripts, abstracts complexity for end users, and enforces security, auditing, and delegation policies. The session highlighted how ScriptRunner simplifies repetitive operational tasks by transforming PowerShell scripts into controlled, role-based services that can be executed via dashboards, web interfaces, or integrations—without granting end users direct administrative rights. We also covered how ScriptRunner improves maintainability with versioning, reporting, logging, and team collaboration features, reducing the risk of human error and ensuring compliance. Ultimately, the key takeaway is that while manual PowerShell remains valuable for development, troubleshooting, and one-off tasks, ScriptRunner is the better choice for standardized, scalable, and secure automation across an organization.

sessions.title: Building a Fully Serverless AI Web App with Azure Cloud-Native Services
sessions.abstract: This presentation demonstrates how to build a fully serverless, AI-powered web application using Azure’s cloud-native services. The solution integrates Azure Static Web Apps, Azure Functions, Azure AI Foundry, and Azure AI Search to deliver intelligent, scalable, and responsive user experiences. By adopting a pay-as-you-go model with no licensing requirements, this architecture ensures cost efficiency and flexibility for developers and organizations alike. Attendees will see an example for how to design, deploy, and manage an end-to-end AI web app that leverages Azure’s modern, cloud-native ecosystem for agility and innovation.

sessions.title: Transforming Enterprise Knowledge: SharePoint Integrated with Azure AI Search and Copilot Studio for Deep Reasoning Insights
sessions.abstract: In this session, we will walk through how to transform standard SharePoint document libraries into an AI-powered knowledge system using Azure AI Search and Copilot Studio. You’ll learn how to build an end-to-end pipeline: ingesting and chunking documents from SharePoint, creating a vectorized Azure AI Search index, and connecting it to Copilot Studio for deep reasoning and grounded responses. The session includes a full live demo showing the journey from SharePoint → Azure Blob Storage → Azure AI Search → Copilot Studio, demonstrating how documents flow through each stage, become searchable vectors, and ultimately power intelligent, reference-backed answers in your Copilot.

sessions.title: Microsoft Entra: The awakening of Identity with a capital I
sessions.abstract: After the Solorigate attack, Microsoft realized that identity was a cornerstone and one of the main vectors for attacks. Attacks on identity have multiplied (via AD FS, via machine identities, etc.). Microsoft Entra provides a new portfolio of solutions designed to address various identity-related challenges. Let's take a look!

sessions.title: Why AI Agent Adoption Needs a Framework
sessions.abstract:
Why AI Agent Adoption Needs a Framework: A Practical Introduction Using Microsoft’s Cloud Adoption Framework
AI agents are rapidly becoming part of core business operations, supporting productivity, analytics, security, and customer engagement. As adoption accelerates, many organizations deploy AI agents faster than their governance, compliance, and operating models can mature. This often results in fragmented implementations, increased risk, and challenges when scaling AI across the enterprise.
This session explains why AI agent adoption requires a structured framework, and how Microsoft’s Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) provides a clear, Microsoft-validated approach for adopting AI agents in a secure, compliant, and scalable way.
Designed as a beginner-friendly technical session, it starts with fundamentals. Attendees will gain a clear understanding of what AI agents are, how they differ from traditional AI workloads, and why they introduce new requirements for architecture, security, and lifecycle management. The session then introduces the AI Agent Adoption Guidance, a newly published addition to CAF, created based on real customer and partner adoption challenges.
The session walks through the four stages of AI agent adoption defined in the guidance:
• Plan for agents: Identify high-value use cases, select appropriate technologies, prepare teams, and ensure data readiness for scale and governance
• Govern and secure agents: Establish governance, security, and…

sessions.title: Building AI Agents with Microsoft Copilot Studio
sessions.abstract: This session introduces how to design, build, and deploy intelligent AI agents using Microsoft Copilot Studio. Attendees will learn how to create conversational agents that connect to data, automate workflows, and integrate seamlessly with Microsoft 365 and external systems without needing deep coding expertise. The session covers key concepts, real-world use cases, and best practices to help you build AI agents that are practical, secure, and business ready.

sessions.title: Building Agentic Business Processes in Microsoft Foundry
sessions.abstract: In this talk, we are going to explore the different ways to build agentic business processes in Microsoft Foundry using the different workflow tools that exist including Foundry Workflows and Azure Logic Apps.
